scope: Linux x64 temporary files/directories in ordinary Lean. Ten parity cases plus one safe-error check per JavaScript engine, in both packaged and full compilers; six unchanged upstream IO regressions. No complete JavaScript suite or native Windows/macOS parity is claimed.
repair: POSIX mkostemp/mkstemp and mkdtemp use the original tmp.XXXXXXXX template and atomic exclusive creation. The adapter preserves symlink/dot segments and relative spelling, retains the instance cwd for pending operations, honors first-present TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP/TEMPDIR including empty values, and returns libuv error codes/messages.
nativeDefect: Pinned native createTempFile crashes with SIGSEGV for a missing temporary directory: lean_decode_uv_error(UV_ENOENT, nullptr) dereferences its null filename. The full comparison records this as a native defect, not a parity pass. Lasm returns the structured ENOENT produced by native Lean in the empty-TMPDIR case, whose filename argument is valid. This is an intentional upstream-bug difference, not a fundamental JavaScript limitation.

limitations: Windows retains the earlier temporary-file adapter and needs a separate repair and validation.
The POSIX implementation is not yet validated on native macOS or ARM64.
Raw non-UTF8 environment variables and near-limit relative paths need separate investigation.
Full Bun uses the local rebuilt capacity8g engine and Linux stack helper; the packaged tests use stock Bun.
Full engine campaigns and integration of the full runtime into the package remain open.
